STARBOUND – Flame in Freefall

Fire behaves differently in microgravity than on Earth. Without normal convection, flames, oxygen transport, and smoke movement change, creating challenges for spacecraft fire safety.

Developed by Çorumun Leblebileri for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, STARBOUND is an interactive educational website that makes NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to understand.

The website introduces NASA experiments such as BASS-II, SAFFIRE, and FLEX. It includes a comparison of Earth gravity (1g) and microgravity (0g), a NASA Experiment Library, research evidence, and an interactive Scenario Explorer.

Users can select oxygen concentration, airflow, fuel type, and gravity conditions. STARBOUND uses transparent, rule-based logic to interpret these selections and present relevant scientific context.

STARBOUND is an independent student project, not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA. It does not use AI/ML, live NASA data connections, or a validated fire-risk model. It does not calculate ignition probability or predict real fire emergencies.

Our mission is to make space combustion research more accessible, understandable, and interactive, supporting scientific curiosity about safer future space exploration.

STARBOUND – Exploring Fire Safety Beyond Earth.

PROJECT DETAILS – STARBOUND

1. Project Overview

STARBOUND is an interactive educational web application created by the team Çorumun Leblebileri for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project focuses on understanding combustion behavior in microgravity and making NASA's space combustion research more accessible.

The website brings together information about NASA experiments and an interactive Scenario Explorer. Users can select different environmental conditions and explore qualitative explanations of how these conditions relate to combustion behavior in space.

2. Main Features

NASA Experiment Library

STARBOUND introduces important NASA combustion research programs, including:

  • BASS and BASS-II: Research on burning and suppression of solid materials in microgravity.
  • SAFFIRE: Experiments investigating fire behavior in spacecraft environments.
  • FLEX: Research on flame behavior and liquid-droplet combustion.
  • ACME: Experiments exploring combustion processes in microgravity.

The website provides scientific context and references to NASA research sources, including the NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS).

Gravity Comparison

The website explains the conceptual differences between combustion under normal Earth gravity (1g) and microgravity (0g). It highlights the role of natural convection and how its reduction changes flame behavior.

Interactive Scenario Explorer

Users can select different conditions to explore:

  • Oxygen concentration
  • Airflow
  • Fuel type
  • Gravity conditions

These inputs allow users to examine different hypothetical combustion scenarios.

Rule-Based Scenario Interpretation

After selecting the conditions, users can update the scenario analysis. The website uses predefined rules to generate qualitative explanations based on the selected inputs and relevant scientific context.

The system is transparent and rule-based. It does not use an AI model or generate numerical fire-risk predictions.

Research Evidence and Safety Context

STARBOUND presents relevant research findings and explains the limitations of available scientific information. It helps users understand the relationship between experimental research and space fire safety.

3. Scientific Approach and Data Sources

Our project is based on publicly available NASA research and scientific documentation.

We use NASA research programs such as BASS-II, SAFFIRE, and FLEX to introduce different aspects of combustion in microgravity.

We also distinguish between different experimental conditions and fuel types. For example, solid-fuel combustion research and liquid-droplet combustion research are presented in their appropriate scientific contexts rather than being treated as identical experiments.

Our goal is to communicate scientific findings accurately while making them understandable to a wider audience.

4. Example of User Interaction

A user can select a BASS-II scenario with 21% oxygen concentration, 0 cm/s airflow, SIBAL cotton/fiberglass fuel, and microgravity (0g).

STARBOUND then interprets the selected conditions using its rule-based system and displays relevant explanations and research context.

This example demonstrates how the website turns user-selected conditions into an educational exploration of microgravity combustion research.

5. Technical Implementation

STARBOUND is implemented as a browser-based web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

  • HTML structures the website and its content.
  • CSS provides the visual design and responsive layout.
  • JavaScript manages user inputs, scenario selection, and rule-based interpretation.

The application can operate as an offline educational tool. It does not require a live connection to NASA systems, external AI services, or real-time spacecraft data.

6. Project Limitations

STARBOUND is an independent educational student project. It is not developed, certified, or endorsed by NASA.

The Scenario Explorer is not a validated fire-risk calculator or a physical combustion simulation. It does not calculate ignition probability, fire severity, flame-spread rates, or crew risk. Its outputs must not be used for real spacecraft operations or emergency decisions.

We clearly communicate these limitations to ensure that users understand the educational purpose of the project.

7. Future Improvements

Potential future improvements include expanding the NASA experiment library, adding more research-based scenarios, improving data visualization, and incorporating additional scientific explanations.

These developments could make STARBOUND a more comprehensive educational platform for exploring combustion science and fire safety in space.

Conclusion

STARBOUND connects NASA's microgravity combustion research with an interactive educational experience. By allowing users to explore experimental conditions and understand scientific context, our project aims to make space fire safety research more accessible and encourage interest in safer future space exploration.

STARBOUND – Exploring Fire Safety Beyond Earth.
